newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares close firmer, hit new record high.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares close firmer, hit new record high.

text.p: Milan shares touched new record highs on Friday closing sharply firmer buoyed by Wall Street, higher domestic bonds and the lira, while the German-Italian summit tried to settle worries over Italy's EMU entry.

U.S. stocks climbed after jobs and earnings data there helped calm worries over a rise in U.S. interest rates pushing the Mib30 to a new record high in early afternoon, while Prime Minister Romano Prodi and German Chancellor Helmut Kohl attempted to sooth rattled markets over Italy's EMU entry.
The blue chip Mib30 index hit a fresh record high of 19,103 before ending the day up 2.06 percent at 19,102.
The Mib30 was set at 10,000 at the end of 1992, while its previous high was on January 23 this year at 19,061. The all-share Mibtel index ended up 1.86 percent at 12,799.

However, equity strategists pointed out that the BCI index which is calculated after the market has closed, ended February 6 at 789.63, well off its peak of 908.20 in May 1986. This, more historic market index, was set at 100 in 1972.

Dealers said the market is liquidity driven at the moment with investors shifting to equities from lower yielding bonds. December and January data showed net inflows of money into these managed funds after two years of outflows.

On individual stocks, Olivetti was one share to underperform the market after its recent run up and ended off 0.48 percent at 664.4 percent. Imminent entry of France Telecom into Infostrada already priced into the stock, dealers say.
Shares in financial holding Gemina only up 0.1 percent at 1,007 lire as analysts judged the pricing of it HPI industrial division, which is to be spun off, as "prudent".
Most other stocks increased in line with the overall stock market, ENI up 0.73 percent at 9,255 lire and Fiat 1.18 percent higher at 5,338 lire, while Parmalat rose 4.2 percent to 2,729 lire.
